mainTopic: The ברכות of the ראש השנה מוסף: their order, their sources, where the שופר is blown, and how many and which פסוקים are said
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the earlier discussion about the תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Then a new משנה sets out the order of the nine ברכות in the ראש השנה מוסף. רבי יוחנן בן נורי puts מלכיות with קדושת השם, with no שופר blowing. רבי עקיבא puts it with קדושת היום and blows for it. A ברייתא gives sources from תהלים and ויקרא for the ברכות, and argues about where מלכיות comes from and which ברכה holds קדושת היום. A story from אושא shows which practice was used in יבנה, and the גמרא explains what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agreed to and what 'the second day' means. A second משנה requires ten פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. The גמרא explains where the number ten comes from, and shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's minimum of three means three in total for each ברכה. The הלכה follows him. A third משנה begins: no פסוקים about punishment, and the פסוקים start with the תורה and end with the נביאים.

steps.title: Closing the previous discussion: the teacher set up the student's תקנה in his own name
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier discussion explain that one תקנה was really made by the student. His teacher, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, established it under his own name, so it is counted as one of his תקנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his teacher established it in his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier discussion about how many תקנות רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made. It explains why one of them still counts as his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why a certain תקנה is counted among רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's even though his student came up with it. The answer is that the teacher formally set it in place. That makes it officially his.

keyTerms.meaning: He established it / set it in place

phrases.english: And his teacher established it in his name.
phrases.notes: His teacher here is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The student made the ruling, and his teacher set it up officially.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַבְעֵיהּ רַבֵּיהּ בִּשְׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous daf about counting רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תקנה officially established by the teacher counts as the teacher's, even if the student came up with it.

steps.title: The order of the מוסף ברכות according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, מלכיות is joined to קדושת השם with no שופר blowing. Then come קדושת היום, זכרונות and שופרות, and the שופר is blown after each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of the blessings: One says אבות, גבורות and קדושת השם, and includes מלכיות with them, and does not blow the שופר. Then he says קדושת היום and blows, זכרונות and blows, שופרות and blows. Then he says עבודה, הודאה and ברכת כהנים. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It lists the order of the ברכות in the ראש השנה מוסף according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and marks where the שופר is blown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal first three ברכות stay the same, but מלכיות is folded into the third one, קדושת השם. Because of that, no שופר is blown at מלכיות. The שופר is blown after קדושת היום, after זכרונות and after שופרות, so there are still three sets of blowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingship: the ברכה with פסוקים about ה׳ as King
Remembrances: the ברכה with פסוקים about ה׳ remembering
The ברכה with פסוקים that mention the שופר
The ברכה about the holiness of the day

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view the שופר is still blown three times. The three times are just at קדושת היום, זכרונות and שופרות, not at מלכיות.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The order of the blessings:
phrases.notes: He means the ברכות of the מוסף on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: One recites Patriarchs and Mighty Deeds
and Sanctification of the Name,
and includes Kingship with them,
phrases.notes: "With them" here means inside the ברכה of קדושת השם.

phrases.english: and he does not blow the shofar.
Sanctification of the Day, and he blows;
Remembrances, and he blows; Shofarot, and he blows;
and he recites Service and Thanksgiving
and the Priestly Blessing.
These are the words of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵדֶר בְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלכיות is joined to קדושת השם without שופר blowing. The שופר is blown after קדושת היום, זכרונות and שופרות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks: why mention מלכיות if you don't blow for it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי יוחנן בן נורי. If no שופר is blown for מלכיות, what is the point of saying it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If he does not blow for מלכיות, why does he mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order. He is setting up his own order, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא assumes that the special ברכות of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות exist to go along with the blowing of the שופר. Each one should have blowing attached to it. Saying מלכיות with no blowing makes it seem pointless.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If he does not blow the shofar for Kingship,
why does he mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם אֵינוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לְמַלְכִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule that מלכיות is said with קדושת השם without blowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלכיות should have שופר blowing attached to it, just like זכרונות and שופרות. Saying it without blowing has no purpose.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's order: מלכיות goes with קדושת היום, and the שופר is blown
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives his own order. The first three ברכות stay as usual, and מלכיות is joined to קדושת היום with שופר blowing. Then come זכרונות and שופרות with blowing, and finally עבודה, הודאה and ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one says אבות, גבורות and קדושת השם, and includes מלכיות with קדושת היום and blows. Then זכרונות and blows, שופרות and blows. Then he says עבודה, הודאה and ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא now gives his own order, which solves his own question. מלכיות is moved so that the שופר is blown for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change is where מלכיות goes. It moves from קדושת השם (no blowing) into קדושת היום (with blowing). Now each of the three special themes, מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות, has its own set of blowing.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה about the Temple service (רצה)

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree there are three sets of שופר blowing in מוסף. They argue only about where מלכיות goes. For רבי יוחנן בן נורי it goes with קדושת השם, with no blowing. For רבי עקיבא it goes with קדושת היום, with blowing.
steps.whyThisMatters: Our מוסף of ראש השנה follows רבי עקיבא's order, with מלכיות said inside the ברכה of קדושת היום.

phrases.english: Rather: one recites Patriarchs and Mighty Deeds
and Sanctification of the Name,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוֹלֵל מַלְכִיּוֹת עִם קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם וְתוֹקֵעַ,
phrases.english: and includes Kingship with Sanctification of the Day, and he blows;
Remembrances, and he blows; Shofarot, and he blows;
and he recites Service and Thanksgiving and the Priestly Blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אוֹמֵר אָבוֹת וּגְבוּרוֹת וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא gives his own order, which answers the challenge he raised in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלכיות is joined to קדושת היום and the שופר is blown for it. The שופר is also blown after זכרונות and after שופרות.

steps.title: The גמרא questions רבי עקיבא's challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's question from the משנה and attacks it. The תורה itself commands us to mention מלכיות, so how can anyone ask why we mention it?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי עקיבא said to him: if he does not blow for מלכיות, why does he mention it? Why does he mention it?! The תורה said to mention it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי עקיבא's words from the משנה and then asks how that question even makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, רבי עקיבא seems to be saying that without שופר blowing there is no reason to say מלכיות. But mentioning מלכיות is a command from the תורה whether or not the שופר is blown. So his question cannot mean what it seems to mean.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Mentions, says (here: says the ברכה of מלכיות)
Literally 'the Merciful One', meaning ה׳ or the תורה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If he does not blow for Kingship,
why does he mention it?
Why does he mention it?!
The Merciful One said: mention!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָה הוּא מַזְכִּיר?! רַחֲמָנָא אָמַר אַידְכַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing רבי עקיבא's challenge from the משנה (Step 3).
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of רבי עקיבא's question, 'why mention מלכיות?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning מלכיות is a command of the תורה that does not depend on שופר blowing, so you cannot ask why it is said.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא meant: why ten verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reexplains רבי עקיבא's question. He was not asking why we say מלכיות. He was asking why it gets the full ten פסוקים when it is already different because it has no שופר blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: why ten? Let him say nine, since it is already different, let it be different!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by showing what רבי עקיבא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every special ברכה normally has ten פסוקים. רבי עקיבא's point is that if רבי יוחנן בן נורי already treats מלכיות differently by not blowing for it, it should also be different in its number of פסוקים. Why give it the full ten, like the ברכות that do have blowing, when nine would be enough?

keyTerms.meaning: Since it already changed, let it change (in other ways too)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's question is not 'why say מלכיות?' It is 'why give it all ten פסוקים if it is already treated differently?'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא doubts that מלכיות must be said. Everyone agrees the תורה requires it. The argument is only about how it fits into the תפילה.

phrases.english: Rather: why ten?
phrases.notes: Ten פסוקים, like each of the other special ברכות of ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Let him say nine,
since it is different, let it be different!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לָמָה עֶשֶׂר? לֵימָא תֵּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 by reinterpreting רבי עקיבא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא was asking why we say מלכיות at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking why מלכיות keeps ten פסוקים if it already differs by having no שופר blowing.

steps.title: Verses behind the first three blessings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a source from תהלים for each of the first three ברכות of the עמידה: אבות, גבורות and קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: from where do we know to say אבות? From 'Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty.' From where גבורות? From 'Give to ה׳ glory and strength.' From where קדושות? From 'Give to ה׳ the glory of His name, bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא that finds a פסוק for each of the first three ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three phrases from the opening of מזמור כט are matched to the three opening ברכות. 'Sons of the mighty' points to the אבות, 'glory and strength' points to ה׳'s גבורות, and 'the glory of His name' and 'holiness' point to קדושת השם.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ברכה, about the forefathers
The second ברכה, about ה׳'s might
The third ברכה, about ה׳'s holiness

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that one says Patriarchs?
As it says: "Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty."
phrases.notes: תהלים כט:א

phrases.english: And from where that one says Mighty Deeds?
As it says: "Give to ה׳ glory and strength."
And from where that one says Holiness?
As it says: "Give to ה׳ the glory of His name,
bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness."
phrases.notes: תהלים כט:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that gives the sources for the ברכות whose order the משנה discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבות, גבורות and קדושות are each based on a phrase from תהלים כט.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source for the special ראש השנה ברכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר takes the פסוק 'שבתון זכרון תרועה מקרא קדש' and links each word to a part of ראש השנה: קדושת היום, זכרונות, שופרות, and not doing מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know to say מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות? רבי אליעזר says: it is written 'a solemn rest, a remembrance of blasts, a holy gathering.' 'Solemn rest' is קדושת היום, 'remembrance' is זכרונות, 'blasts' is שופרות, and 'holy gathering' means make the day holy by not doing מלאכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the special ראש השנה ברכות, and רבי אליעזר links them to one פסוק, word by word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the four phrases gets one job. שבתון gives קדושת היום, זכרון gives זכרונות, תרועה gives שופרות, and מקרא קדש teaches the ban on מלאכה. The question also asks about מלכיות, but רבי אליעזר does not say where it comes from. Steps 12 and 13 bring sources for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה about ה׳ as King
The ברכה about the holiness of the day

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one says Kingship, Remembrances and Shofarot?
Rabbi Eliezer says: as it is written,
"A solemn rest, a remembrance of blasts, a holy gathering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:כד, the פסוק about ראש השנה.

phrases.english: "Solemn rest": this is the Sanctity of the Day;
"remembrance": these are Remembrances;
"blasts": these are Shofarot;
"a holy gathering":
make it holy with regard to doing work.
phrases.notes: He means: make the day holy by not doing forbidden work on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מַלְכִיּוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, moving from the first three ברכות to the special ראש השנה ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ויקרא כג:כד, שבתון = קדושת היום, זכרון = זכרונות, תרועה = שופרות, מקרא קדש = no מלאכה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא questions רבי אליעזר's matching
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks why the word שבתון should not mean resting from work. It is the first word of the פסוק, and the word itself means rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: why don't we say that שבתון means resting, since the פסוק opens with it first!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא challenges how רבי אליעזר matched the words of the פסוק to their meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שבתון comes from 'rest', and it opens the פסוק. So it makes the most sense for it to teach the basic rule of the day, resting from מלאכה. רבי אליעזר instead used it for קדושת היום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
For what reason should we not say
"solemn rest" means resting,
since the verse opened with it first!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אליעזר's reading in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading of שבתון as קדושת היום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבתון means rest and comes first in the פסוק, so it should teach the ban on מלאכה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's own reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא matches the words differently. שבתון means not doing מלאכה, and מקרא קדש is קדושת היום. זכרון and תרועה stay the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'solemn rest' means make it holy by not doing work; 'remembrance' is זכרונות; 'blasts' is שופרות; 'holy gathering' is קדושת היום.
steps.whatsHappening: After his challenge, רבי עקיבא gives his own way to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from רבי אליעזר is that the first and last phrases switch jobs. שבתון now teaches resting from מלאכה, and מקרא קדש now gives קדושת היום. Both still read זכרון as זכרונות and תרועה as שופרות.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy gathering, here read as קדושת היום

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא both learn זכרונות and שופרות from this פסוק. They argue only about which word gives קדושת היום and which gives the ban on מלאכה.

phrases.english: Rather: "solemn rest":
make it holy with regard to doing work;
"remembrance": these are Remembrances;
"blasts": these are Shofarot;
"a holy gathering": this is the Sanctity of the Day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״שַׁבָּתוֹן״ — קַדְּשֵׁהוּ בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following his challenge in Step 9, רבי עקיבא offers a different reading in place of רבי אליעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ויקרא כג:כד, שבתון = no מלאכה, זכרון = זכרונות, תרועה = שופרות, מקרא קדש = קדושת היום.

steps.title: What is the source for saying מלכיות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that מלכיות must be said on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that we say מלכיות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a תורה source for the ברכה of מלכיות. This line sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps gave sources for זכרונות and שופרות from the words of the ראש השנה פסוק. That פסוק has no word for kingship, so the גמרא now looks for a separate source for מלכיות.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (a request for a source)
The ברכה about ה׳ being King, with ten פסוקים about kingship

phrases.english: From where do we know that we say Kingships?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מַלְכִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier steps found sources for the other ברכות. Now the גמרא looks for the missing one, מלכיות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A תורה source showing that מלכיות must be said on ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבי learns מלכיות from 'I am ה׳ your God'
steps.stepSummary: רבי points to 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' written just before the ראש השנה פסוק and says this is מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי says, the פסוק says 'I am ה׳ your God,' and then 'In the seventh month.' This is kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question. The words 'I am ה׳ your God' come right before the פסוקים about ראש השנה, so they teach us to speak about ה׳'s kingship on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' means accepting ה׳ as our King. Since it sits right next to 'בחדש השביעי' in the תורה, רבי connects the two. So kingship belongs to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
I am ה׳ your God, an expression of ה׳'s rule over us

phrases.english: It was taught: Rebbi says:
"I am ה׳ your God"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

phrases.english: and then "In the seventh month": this is Kingship.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:24, two פסוקים after the first one, where the topic of ראש השנה starts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' sit right next to the ראש השנה פסוק, and they mean kingship.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה brings a different source that ties מלכיות to זכרונות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה learns from במדבר that wherever זכרונות are said, מלכיות are said with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: There is no need for that. The פסוק says, 'They will be a remembrance for you before your God; I am ה׳ your God.' The פסוק did not need to add 'I am ה׳ your God.' So why does it say it? It sets a rule: everywhere זכרונות are said, מלכיות should be said with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says רבי's source is not needed. He brings a different פסוק where 'I am ה׳ your God' comes right after the word 'remembrance.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק in במדבר, the words 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' seem extra. רבי יוסי בר יהודה explains that they are there to teach a rule: kingship always goes together with remembrance. Since we already know זכרונות are said on ראש השנה, מלכיות must be said too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (that source is unnecessary)
The פסוק did not need to say this
Built a model, meaning a general rule that applies everywhere

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: It is not needed,
for it says:
"They will be a remembrance for you before your God"
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:10. Right after this, the פסוק ends with 'I am ה׳ your God.'

phrases.english: for the verse did not need to say "I am ה׳ your God",
so why does it say "I am ה׳ your God"?
This sets a model for every place
where remembrances are mentioned:
Kingships should be with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with how רבי found the source in step 12 and gives a different one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra words 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' after 'לזכרון' teach that מלכיות always go together with זכרונות.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that מלכיות are said. They only disagree about which פסוק teaches it.

steps.title: Which ברכה holds קדושת היום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which ברכה of the ראש השנה מוסף we mention קדושת היום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where does one say the holiness of the day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question of where in the עמידה we put קדושת היום. This line sets up two opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה the מוסף has nine ברכות: three at the start, three in the middle (מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות), and three at the end. In this ברייתא, קדושת היום does not get its own ברכה, so it has to be joined to one of the middle ones. The question is which one.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the day, the part of the עמידה about the special day

phrases.english: And where does one say the holiness of the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָן אוֹמְרָהּ לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of the ברכות to the order they are said in.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה in the ראש השנה מוסף holds קדושת היום.

steps.title: רבי: קדושת היום goes with מלכיות in the fourth ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי says קדושת היום is said together with מלכיות, because everywhere else it is in the fourth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי says, one says it with מלכיות. Just as everywhere else we find it in the fourth ברכה, here too it is in the fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that קדושת היום is joined to מלכיות. He reasons that on every שבת and יום טוב, קדושת היום is the fourth ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלכיות is the fourth ברכה on ראש השנה. Putting קדושת היום there keeps it in the fourth spot, the same as on every other holy day.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we find (comparing to other cases)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rebbi says:
One says it with the Kingships.
Just as we find everywhere that it is in the fourth blessing,
so too here, in the fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: עִם הַמַּלְכִיּוֹת אוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With מלכיות, so that קדושת היום stays in the fourth ברכה as on other holy days.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: קדושת היום goes with זכרונות in the middle
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says קדושת היום goes with זכרונות, because everywhere else it is the middle ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One says it with זכרונות. Just as everywhere else we find it in the middle, here too it is in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with רבי. He says the rule is not 'the fourth ברכה' but 'the middle ברכה,' and on ראש השנה the middle one is זכרונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there are seven ברכות, so the fourth is also the middle one. Both opinions fit that case, so the two תנאים are really arguing about what the pattern is. On ראש השנה there are nine ברכות, so the middle is the fifth, which is זכרונות.
steps.confusionAlert: On a regular שבת or יום טוב, 'fourth' and 'middle' are the same ברכה. They only become different on ראש השנה, because its מוסף has nine ברכות.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי puts קדושת היום with מלכיות (the fourth ברכה). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל puts it with זכרונות (the fifth, which is the middle of nine).

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One says it with the Remembrances.
Just as we find everywhere that it is in the middle,
so too here, in the middle.
phrases.notes: On ראש השנה there are nine ברכות, so the middle one is the fifth, זכרונות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת אוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי's answer in step 15, using the same kind of comparison but a different pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדושת היום is said with זכרונות, because the pattern everywhere is the middle ברכה.

steps.title: In אושא, a חזן follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי and is told it was not done that way
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells a story. In אושא, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא led the מוסף and arranged it like רבי יוחנן בן נורי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל told him this was not the practice in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the בית דין set the year in אושא, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא led the prayers in front of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and followed רבי יוחנן בן נורי. רבן שמעון said to him: 'In יבנה they did not do it this way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a real-life story to show which way of arranging the ברכות was actually practiced. Here the first חזן's way gets rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי puts מלכיות together with the third ברכה, the holiness of ה׳'s Name. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects by pointing to how things were done in יבנה. The way it was done in יבנה is treated as the correct practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in the גליל where the סנהדרין met after יבנה
The earlier seat of the סנהדרין, whose way of doing things is treated as the standard
Literally 'went down'; here it means he led the prayers as חזן
Fixed the calendar year (set the months)

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: And when the court sanctified the year in Usha,
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka went down
phrases.notes: 'Went down' means he stepped forward to lead the prayers. The חזן stood in a lower spot in front of the ark.

phrases.english: before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and he did like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
Rabban Shimon said to him:
They were not accustomed to do this in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a story showing how the dispute about arranging the ברכות played out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי יוחנן בן נורי's arrangement was not the practice in יבנה.

steps.title: A second prayer leader follows רבי עקיבא and is approved
steps.stepSummary: On 'the second day', רבי חנינא, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, led the prayers like רבי עקיבא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said this is how it was done in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day, רבי חנינא the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי led the prayers and followed רבי עקיבא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: 'This is how they did it in יבנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues, and this time רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approves of what the חזן did. This sets up the next question the גמרא will ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא puts מלכיות together with קדושת היום, and he blows שופר for it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's approval is surprising, because in Step 16 he held that קדושת היום goes with זכרונות, not with מלכיות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the second day'; the גמרא will soon ask what this means
'This is how they used to do it', meaning approval of the practice

phrases.english: On the second day there went down

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGlili,
and he did like Rabbi Akiva.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
This is how they were accustomed to do in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי יָרַד רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the story: a different arrangement, this time approved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that רבי עקיבא's way of doing it matched the practice in יבנה.

steps.title: How can רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approve of רבי עקיבא's way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved of רבי עקיבא's way. He himself said that קדושת היום goes with זכרונות, not with מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי עקיבא? But רבי עקיבא said מלכיות goes with קדושת היום, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said קדושת היום goes with זכרונות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved of a practice he seems to disagree with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא, these two תנאים gave different placements for קדושת היום. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved of רבי עקיבא's way completely, he would be going against his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?', which opens a surprised question
'But surely...', which brings a source that contradicts

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
holds like Rabbi Akiva?
But didn't Rabbi Akiva say:

phrases.aramaic: מַלְכִיּוֹת עִם קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם אָמַר לְהוּ,
phrases.english: One says Kingship together with the Holiness of the Day,
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת אָמַר לְהוּ?
phrases.english: One says the Holiness of the Day together with Remembrances?
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion from Step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the approval from Step 18 by setting it against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own opinion in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement 'כך היו נוהגין ביבנה' about רבי עקיבא's way
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He cannot approve of putting מלכיות with קדושת היום, because he himself holds that קדושת היום goes with זכרונות.

steps.title: רבי זירא: he only agreed about blowing שופר for מלכיות
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only agreed with one part of רבי עקיבא's practice: that we blow שופר for מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: He meant to say that we blow שופר for מלכיות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the contradiction. The approval was only about one detail, not the whole arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's practice had two parts: where to put מלכיות, and blowing שופר for it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agreed only with the שופר part, so he never gave up his own view about where קדושת היום goes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To say', meaning he only meant to say this one point
We blow שופר for the ברכה of מלכיות

steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'this is how they did it in יבנה' backs only the blowing of שופר for מלכיות, not putting מלכיות together with קדושת היום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
To say that we blow the shofar for Kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לוֹמַר שֶׁתּוֹקְעִין לְמַלְכִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by narrowing what the approval covered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved of the whole of רבי עקיבא's arrangement.
steps.terutzMaskana: He approved only of blowing שופר for מלכיות.

steps.title: What does 'on the second day' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the words 'on the second day' from the story and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On the second day רבי חנינא led the prayers.' What does 'second' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the story to make its meaning clear. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear whether 'second day' means the second day of ראש השנה or something else. The answer depends on how the calendar worked back then.

phrases.english: "On the second day Rabbi Chanina went down."
What is "second"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לַיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי יָרַד רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַאי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבן שמעון בן גמליאל question and goes back to a word in the story itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which 'second day' the ברייתא is talking about.

steps.title: It cannot mean the second day of יום טוב, because אלול was never made full
steps.stepSummary: If 'second day' meant the second day of ראש השנה, then אלול would have been made a 30-day month. But since עזרא, אלול was never made full.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the second day of יום טוב, does that mean they made אלול a full month? But רבי חנינא בר כהנא said that from the days of עזרא onward, we never found אלול made full!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious reading and shows that it doesn't work, because of a fact about the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first day of ראש השנה to have turned out to be just the 30th of אלול, אלול would have needed a 30th day. רבי חנינא בר כהנא says this never happened after עזרא, so this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say...', which brings up a possible reading
They made it full (gave the month 30 days)
An אלול with 30 days instead of 29

steps.confusionAlert: 'Second day' here does not simply mean the second of two set days of ראש השנה. The גמרא is assuming that this reading would require אלול to have had a 30th day.

phrases.english: If you say the second day of Yom Tov,
is that to say they made Elul full?!
phrases.notes: Then the first day they kept would have been the 30th of אלול, and the real first of תשרי would be the 'second day'.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana say:
From the days of Ezra onward
we have not found Elul made full!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי לְמֵימְרָא דְּעַבְּרוּהּ לֶאֱלוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in Step 21 and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'second day' as the second day of ראש השנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would mean אלול was made full, which רבי חנינא בר כהנא says never happened after עזרא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: 'second' means ראש השנה of the next year
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'the second day' means the next time ראש השנה came, the following year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is 'second'? The second time, the next year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the right reading. The two חזנים led on two different ראש השנה's, one year apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the problem with אלול goes away. The story covers two years in a row in אושא.
steps.whatToRemember: The two stories in אושא happened on ראש השנה of two different years, not on two days of the same ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is "second"?
On the second [Rosh Hashanah] day, in the following year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מַאי שֵׁנִי לְיוֹם שֵׁנִי לַשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 with a reading that avoids the problem raised in Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Second day' means the second day of the same ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Second day' means ראש השנה of the following year.

steps.title: משנה: ten פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that we should not say fewer than ten פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says three of each is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not say fewer than ten מלכיות, ten זכרונות and ten שופרות. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: if he said three of each, he has done his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from the order of the ברכות to how many פסוקים go into each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets ten פסוקים as the minimum for each of the three special ברכות. רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees and says that, at least once it has already been done, three of each counts.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not go below (this minimum)
The ברכה of פסוקים about the שופר

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is where the number of פסוקים in the ראש השנה מוסף comes from. The גמרא will next look into where the number ten comes from.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
We do not say fewer than ten Kingship verses,
than ten Remembrance verses, than ten Shofar verses.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
If he said three of each of them,
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֲשָׂרָה מַלְכִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject: how many פסוקים go into each ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion requires at least ten פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says three of each is enough.

steps.title: What do the ten verses stand for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the ten פסוקים of מלכיות correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These ten פסוקים of מלכיות, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking why the number is ten. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said not to say fewer than ten פסוקים, but it did not say why ten. The גמרא assumes a number like this must be based on something, and asks for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: The section of the מוסף prayer of ראש השנה about ה׳'s Kingship
Corresponding to what? (What does this stand for?)

phrases.english: GEMARA: These ten verses of Kingship,
what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי עֲשָׂרָה מַלְכִיּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the number ten taught in the משנה of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or symbolic basis for the number ten.

steps.title: רבי: the ten praises of דוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the ten פסוקים match the ten praises דוד said in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: They correspond to the ten praises that דוד said in ספר תהלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives the first answer: the ten פסוקים stand for ten praises of ה׳ that דוד המלך said in ספר תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praising ה׳ fits these sections of the prayer, so רבי ties the number ten to a set of ten praises. He has not yet told us which praises, and the next step will ask about that.

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: They correspond to the ten praises
that David said in the book of Psalms.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה הִלּוּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים match ten praises in תהלים.

steps.title: But תהלים has many more praises
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ספר תהלים contains far more than ten praises.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are many praises!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי. ספר תהלים is full of praises, so which ten does he mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תהלים has dozens of praises, then the number ten does not stand out. רבי's answer only works if he can point to one specific group of exactly ten.

phrases.english: There are many praises!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלּוּלִים טוּבָא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's claim that there are ten praises
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תהלים has many more than ten praises, so the number ten cannot come from 'the praises' in general.

steps.title: The praises in the chapter of 'הללוהו בתקע שופר'
steps.stepSummary: רבי meant the praises in the chapter that includes 'Praise Him with the blast of the שופר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He means those praises where it is written: 'Praise Him with the blast of the shofar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי meant one specific chapter, the one that says 'Praise Him with the blast of the שופר.' That chapter has exactly ten praises.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This chapter fits very well, because it mentions the שופר, which is the theme of ראש השנה. It also contains exactly ten praises, so the count matches.

phrases.english: Those in which it is written
'Praise Him with the blast of the shofar.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 150:3. This chapter praises ה׳ ten times: 'הללו אל' once and 'הללוהו' nine times, not counting the הללויה at the start and end.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ הַלְלוּהוּ בְּתֵקַע שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the reference to a specific passage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי meant all the praises in תהלים, which are far more than ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the ten praises in the chapter that mentions the שופר.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the עשרת הדברות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ten פסוקים match the עשרת הדברות given at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They correspond to the עשרת הדברות, which were said to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: רב יוסף says the ten פסוקים stand for the עשרת הדברות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף ties the number ten to a different set of ten: the ten commandments heard at סיני. This is another explanation for the number, and it does not argue with the halacha itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
They correspond to the Ten Commandments
that were said to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים match the עשרת הדברות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ten sayings of Creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ten פסוקים match the ten sayings through which the world was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They correspond to the ten utterances through which the world was created.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: רבי יוחנן says the ten פסוקים stand for the ten sayings ה׳ used to create the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer ties the number ten to בריאת העולם. That is fitting, since ראש השנה is linked to the creation of the world. The גמרא will next ask which ten sayings he means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They correspond to the ten utterances
through which the world was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים match the ten sayings of Creation.

steps.title: Which are the ten sayings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ten sayings רבי יוחנן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי יוחנן to identify the ten sayings. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before accepting the answer, we need to know where in the תורה these ten sayings are found.

phrases.english: Which are they?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of רבי יוחנן's answer in step 30.

steps.title: The times it says 'ויאמר'
steps.stepSummary: The ten sayings are the times 'And He said' appears in the Creation story.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He said.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the sayings are the times the תורה says 'And ה׳ said' in the story of Creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא counts the times the תורה writes 'ויאמר' in the Creation story in בראשית. Those are the 'sayings' רבי יוחנן means.

phrases.english: 'And He said.'
phrases.notes: He means each place in the Creation story where the פסוק says 'And ה׳ said.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sayings are the occurrences of 'ויאמר' in the Creation story.

steps.title: But there are only nine 'ויאמר's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'ויאמר' appears only nine times in the Creation story.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'And He said' phrases in בראשית are only nine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. If you count, 'ויאמר' appears only nine times, not ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן needs exactly ten sayings, but the count of 'ויאמר' comes up one short. So either the answer is wrong, or there must be a tenth saying somewhere.

phrases.english: The 'And He said' of Genesis
are only nine!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר דִּבְרֵאשִׁית תִּשְׁעָה הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'ויאמר's add up to ten sayings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the word in בראשית gives only nine, so the number ten does not fit.

steps.title: 'בראשית' itself counts as a saying
steps.stepSummary: The first word 'בראשית' is also a saying, as the פסוק says the heavens were made by ה׳'s word.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the beginning' is also an utterance, as it is written: 'By the word of ה׳ the heavens were made.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opening words 'In the beginning ה׳ created' also count as a saying, which makes ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the word 'ויאמר' does not appear there, a פסוק in תהלים says the heavens were made 'by the word of ה׳.' That shows the first act of Creation was also through a saying, so the total becomes ten.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations for the number ten: the ten praises in the שופר chapter of תהלים (רבי), the עשרת הדברות (רב יוסף), and the ten sayings of Creation, counting 'בראשית' as the tenth (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: 'In the beginning' is also an utterance,
as it is written: 'By the word of ה׳ the heavens were made.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:6

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֵאשִׁית נָמֵי מַאֲמָר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a hidden tenth item backed by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the explicit 'ויאמר's count, which gives nine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בראשית' also counts as a saying, which gives ten.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוחנן בן נורי: three of each
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי יוחנן בן נורי says three of each is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: If one said three from each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה, where רבי יוחנן בן נורי says three of each is enough. It is setting up a question about what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'three three' are not clear. Three of what, from where? This quote sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ מִכּוּלָּן — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he said three from each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the number ten and returns to the second opinion in the משנה of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, saying three of each is enough.

steps.title: Does 'three' mean nine verses or three verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי means three from each section of תנ״ך (nine in total) or one from each section (three in total).
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: How is he teaching? Three from the תורה, three from the נביאים and three from the כתובים, which makes nine, so they differ by only one פסוק? Or perhaps one from the תורה, one from the נביאים and one from the כתובים, which makes three, so they differ by a lot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to read רבי יוחנן בן נורי's words. It lays out two possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: three from each of תורה, נביאים and כתובים, which is nine. Then he argues with the ת״ק, who requires ten, by only one פסוק. Reading two: one from each section, which is three. Then the gap is seven פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised among them
How is he teaching? (What does he mean?)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Three of each' does not obviously mean three פסוקים in total. The whole question is whether 'each' means each section of תנ״ך (nine פסוקים) or each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות (three פסוקים per blessing, one from each section).

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: How is he teaching?

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה, שָׁלֹשׁ מִן הַנְּבִיאִים,
phrases.english: Three from the Torah, three from the Prophets,
and three from the Writings,
which makes nine,
and the difference between them is one?
phrases.notes: 'Between them' means between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the first opinion in the משנה, which requires ten.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: one from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד מִן הַנְּבִיאִים, וְאֶחָד מִן הַכְּתוּבִים —
phrases.english: and one from the Prophets, and one from the Writings,
which makes three,
and the difference between them is a lot?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, הֵיכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the wording quoted in step 35 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'three of each' means nine פסוקים (three per section) or three פסוקים (one per section).
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides the minimum number of פסוקים needed according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, which is either nine or three for each blessing.

steps.title: Bringing a ברייתא that allows seven verses for each blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. Its first opinion requires ten פסוקים for each ברכה, but seven is enough, matching the seven heavens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from a ברייתא: You may not say fewer than ten פסוקים of מלכיות, ten of זכרונות and ten of שופרות. But if you said seven of each, you have fulfilled your obligation, matching the seven heavens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to answer the question from step 36. This first half sets up the proof; the deciding words come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא counts the number of פסוקים in each ברכה as one total: ten ideally, seven at minimum. Seven is matched to the seven heavens, which is a plain count and has nothing to do with sections of תנ״ך. This prepares the reader to see how רבי יוחנן בן נורי counts in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear — the גמרא is bringing a source to settle a question
We do not go below (a certain number)
The three special ברכות of ראש השנה מוסף: Kingship, Remembrance and Shofar

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
One does not say fewer than ten Kingship verses,
fewer than ten Remembrance verses, or fewer than ten Shofar verses.
And if he said seven from each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation,
corresponding to the seven heavens.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing a source to answer the question in step 36
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי's 'three' means three in total for each ברכה or nine
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the numbers are counted as one total for each ברכה

steps.title: Three verses in total, matching three groups
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the minimum is seven, but three is enough after the fact, matching תורה, נביאים, כתובים or כהנים, לוים, ישראלים. So he means three in total for each ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: Someone who says fewer than ten should not go below seven. But if he said three of each, he has fulfilled his obligation, matching תורה, נביאים and כתובים. Some say it matches כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: This half of the ברייתא answers the question. רבי יוחנן בן נורי's 'three' is three פסוקים in total for each ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He first says that someone who goes below ten should not go below seven, and then says three is enough. If 'three' meant nine, it would already be more than seven, so the step down only makes sense if he means three in total. The second reason he gives, כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, is just a group of three and has nothing to do with sections of תנ״ך, which supports this.

keyTerms.meaning: One who goes below (the ideal number)
And some say it this way
The three groups of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'three, matching תורה, נביאים, כתובים' as three from each section, which would be nine. He means three פסוקים total for each ברכה, which can be one from each section.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:
One who says fewer should not say fewer than seven,
but if he said three from each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation,
corresponding to the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: כְּנֶגֶד כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: and some say: corresponding to the priests, the Levites and the Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אָמַר: הַפּוֹחֵת לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשֶּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and gives the decisive wording
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'three of each' means nine פסוקים or three
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three in total for each ברכה, like the 'seven' in the same ברייתא, and matched to groups of three

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: three פסוקים for each ברכה is enough after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 explained what רבי יוחנן בן נורי meant. Now we learn that the practical הלכה follows his opinion, so the minimum is three פסוקים for each ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: רב הונא reporting what his teacher שמואל said

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is ten פסוקים for each ברכה. After the fact, three is enough (רבי יוחנן בן נורי), and the הלכה follows him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical minimum number of פסוקים in each of the three middle ברכות of ראש השנה מוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the opinion just explained
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי: three פסוקים for each ברכה is enough.

steps.title: New משנה: no verses about punishment
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that we do not use זכרון, מלכות or שופר פסוקים that speak about punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not mention פסוקים of Remembrance, Kingship or Shofar that speak about punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches which kinds of פסוקים may not be used in these ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about how many פסוקים to say. Now the משנה adds a rule about what kind: a פסוק that mentions ה׳'s kingship, remembering or the shofar in a setting of punishment may not be used.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One does not mention verses of Remembrance, Kingship,
or Shofar that are about punishment.
phrases.notes: 'About punishment' goes back on all three kinds of פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַזְכִּירִין זִכָּרוֹן מַלְכוּת וְשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל פּוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסוקים about punishment may not be used for מלכיות, זכרונות or שופרות.

steps.title: Begin with the תורה, finish with the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says to begin with פסוקים from the תורה and finish with נביא. רבי יוסי says finishing with the תורה is also acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: You begin with the תורה and finish with a נביא. רבי יוסי says: If you finished with the תורה, you have fulfilled your obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the order of the פסוקים within each ברכה, and רבי יוסי adds a more lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the last פסוק should come from נביא. רבי יוסי agrees that you start with the תורה, but holds that if the last פסוק is also from the תורה, you have still fulfilled your obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the order of the פסוקים we say in each of the three ברכות.

phrases.english: He begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophets.
Rabbi Yosei says:
If he concluded with the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְחִיל בַּתּוֹרָה, וּמַשְׁלִים בַּנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה with a rule about the order of the פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begin with the תורה and finish with נביא. רבי יוסי says finishing with the תורה is also acceptable.
